issues.issue: This introductory description of what Angie's List 'provides' points toward a service of user-experience-based reviews, while Sections 13 and 24 disclaim any warranty as to the accuracy or integrity of that Content. A member could rely on the introduction as an operative promise against those disclaimers.

The definition of 'Service'/'Services' lists named products and then sweeps in 'any other products and services offered by Angie's List at any time', leaving the reach of the catch-all against the enumerated specifics uncertain; the garbled 'vouchers, ordeals' adds to the list's indeterminacy. Every disclaimer and release in the Agreement is keyed to this open-ended defined term.

The Agreement is said to include terms 'in, and linked to' it, but nothing identifies which linked pages are incorporated, so the outer boundary of the contract is undefined. A court could be asked to decide whether a linked policy or webpage is part of the Agreement.

The incorporation of terms merely 'linked to' this Agreement sits awkwardly with Section 29, which declares this Agreement to be the entire agreement superseding all other understandings. The two provisions describe different contract boundaries.

The promise that 'You will receive notice if modifications to the Agreement are made' is hard to square with Section 19, under which modifications are 'effective immediately upon being posted' and the member bears the burden of reviewing the terms regularly. Whether notice is a condition of effectiveness is left open.

Agreeing that other Angie's List sites 'may be governed by separate terms and conditions, agreements and privacy policies' is in tension with the Section 29 entire-agreement clause. Which instrument controls a dispute over website use is not resolved.

The condition reads 'grandfathered members who are renewing and:(1) ... or (2)', so the conjunction 'and' followed by disjunctive numbered alternatives makes the test for grandfathering grammatically uncertain. A member who takes no action and one who affirmatively elects are treated by the same garbled sentence.
'Certain markets' is undefined and unlisted, so which members can select a Plan cannot be determined from the instrument. The date qualifier is precise but the geographic qualifier is not.

The Redeemable Benefit is an annual rebate 'in an amount determined by Angle's List' toward a 'Big Deal, Storefront Offer, SnapFix purchase, or other qualifying transaction', leaving both the value and the qualifying transactions undefined. Neither the amount nor the catch-all category can be applied from the text.

The Premium Plan promises 'Access to Angle's List's Complaint Resolution Process' as a purchased benefit, but Section 11 states that participation in the CRP 'is at Angle's List's sole discretion' and that it may reject a request 'for any reason'. A Premium member denied the CRP could point to a direct conflict.

'Your Angle's List account is in good standing' is undefined nowhere in the Agreement, so the condition on which all Plan benefits depend has no ascertainable content. The garbled 'within cone-year period' further obscures the redemption window.

The promise that a renewed legacy subscription 'will maintain the same services that are currently provided' is difficult to reconcile with Section 1's reservation of the right to modify the Plans at any time and Section 20's right to modify or discontinue the Service. A grandfathered member could read this as a freeze that the other clauses deny.

The unrestricted right to modify the Plans 'at any time and in its sole discretion' cannot easily be squared with the preceding paragraph's assurance that a renewing legacy member's subscription 'will maintain the same services that are currently provided'. One clause promises continuity, the other unilateral change.

Section 3 requires the user to be '18 years of age or older', while Section 16(A) has the user warrant that he or she is 'above the age of eighteen (18)', which literally excludes an eighteen-year-old. The two eligibility statements do not match.

'Membership in the Service is void where prohibited' identifies neither the prohibiting law nor the place, and 'void' is left to do work no other provision explains. The clause is too compressed to apply without construction.

The privacy policy is referenced by URL without stating whether it is incorporated into the Agreement, which matters against the Section 29 entire-agreement clause and the Section 24(D) disclaimer of any warranty that information will not be disclosed. Whether the policy is contractually binding is left open.

The 'Membership Fee' is defined as 'the amount You were charged ... not including any promotions or discounts that may have been applied', which is self-contradictory: the amount actually charged is the discounted amount. Since renewals and the Section 25 liability cap are both measured by this term, the ambiguity has real consequences.

This Section tells the member that subscriptions renew automatically 'UNLESS YOU OPT OUT OF THE AUTOMATIC RENEWAL FEATURE AS PROVIDED BELOW', but no opt-out feature appears anywhere below; only the cancellation paragraph exists. The cross-reference has no referent in the instrument.

Renewal 'AT THE MEMBERSHIP FEE' depends on the Section 6 definition of Membership Fee, which excludes promotions and discounts, so a member who joined at a discount may be renewed at a higher figure than he was charged. The renewal price turns on a defined term that contradicts itself.

As with the monthly paragraph, renewal 'AT THE MEMBERSHIP FEE FOR ANNUAL MEMBERSHIPS' incorporates the Section 6 definition that excludes discounts actually applied, leaving the renewal amount contestable. The clause also permits 180 days of re-attempted billing without stating the effect on the term.

This paragraph says the Additional List feature was available only 'formerly', yet Section 6 still governs payment of 'Additional List Fees' and the following paragraph provides for renewal notice before 'renewing the Additional List'. Whether the feature survives cannot be determined from the instrument as a whole.

'If You received a free offer to access all subscriptions in the Service, Angie's List Health, or Angie's List Classic Car' is a garbled list, and it is unclear whether the free-offer member is renewed at a fee at all. The sentence converts a free offer into a charge without saying so plainly.

Email notice is promised before renewing a free-offer Additional List, whereas the monthly and annual renewal paragraphs state that Angie's List 'will not provide You with any notices prior to each ... renewal payment'. Which regime governs a free-offer subscription is not resolved.

The upgrade mechanic — the first subscription is 'upgraded' yet the member is simultaneously 'purchasing an additional annual subscription' whose term begins later — is internally hard to follow and does not say whether any credit is given for the unexpired term. Two readings of what the member pays are available on the face of the paragraph.

'A refund of the difference between Your current Plan and the new Plan' does not say whether the difference is prorated for the unexpired term or refunded in full, and the upgrade paragraph gives no corresponding rule. The measure of the refund is left to construction.

Cancellation must be 'received' by 5:00 p.m. the business day before renewal, yet Section 28 deems notices to Angie's List delivered on the earlier of verified delivery or two business days after sending. A cancellation mailed in time under Section 28 could be late under this paragraph.

The paragraph says a portion of the Membership Fee ($6.50 per year) 'will be applied towards Your subscription to the magazine' and then that 'the magazine subscription fee is not deductible from Your Membership Fee', which reads as a contradiction about whether the member pays extra. 'Where applicable' further leaves the entitlement uncertain.

'You agree that You shall not bring any action against Angie's List relating in any way to the Incentives' is an absolute covenant not to sue drafted wholly in the drafter's favour, with no carve-out even for Angie's List's own conduct in offering the Incentive. Its reach against, say, a misdescribed incentive is exactly the kind of one-sided ambiguity construed against the drafter.

Permitting use of the account by 'the members of Your household' sits against Section 16(T), by which the member agrees not to 'register for an account on behalf of an individual other than yourself'. The permitted scope of shared use is not clearly reconciled.

The licence bars exploitation 'for any commercial, educational, or any other non-personal purpose', a catch-all appended to two specifics whose reach is uncertain; and the ban on 'visit[ing]' the reviews cuts against the licence to access them just granted. The boundary of permitted 'personal purchase decisions' use is left to construction.

'Any competitors of the Service Providers' is undefined and potentially boundless, since competition is not limited by trade, market or geography. A member could not know which employers or holdings disqualify a review.

'Related (by blood, adoption, marriage, or domestic partnership, if the Service Provider is an individual) in any way' has no degree limit, and the trailing conditional leaves unclear whether the whole representation applies only where the Service Provider is an individual. Both the scope of relatedness and the reach of the parenthetical are contestable.

Disclosure of the reviewer's name and review information to Service Providers may be read against Section 5's privacy policy and Section 15's separate treatment of health information. Whether the policy qualifies this blanket disclosure is unresolved.
'An active, qualifying Plan' is not defined, and nothing in Section 11 says which Plans qualify. The eligibility condition for the CRP therefore cannot be applied from this provision alone.

Removal of a member's review once a Service Provider satisfies the complaint is hard to reconcile with Section 13's characterisation of Angie's List as a 'passive conduit' that does not control Content. The clause has Angie's List editing the ratings pool it elsewhere says it merely carries.

The paragraph breaks off mid-sentence — 'we may ask You to sign a HIPAA ... waiver to allow the Service Provider to discuss the issue with' — so the scope of the HIPAA consent the member gives is textually incomplete. What follows 'with' cannot be supplied from the instrument.

Making CRP participation wholly discretionary and rejectable 'for any reason' contradicts the Premium Plan bullet in Section 1, which sells 'Access to Angle's List's Complaint Resolution Process' as a paid benefit. A paid entitlement and an unfettered discretion to refuse cannot both be given full effect.

The 'irrevocable, perpetual' licence in Content is difficult to reconcile with Section 18, under which termination 'may include the deletion of the Content associated with Your account'. Whether the member's Content survives termination and in whose hands is left unresolved.

'Passive conduit' is an undefined characterisation doing legal work, and it is not stated whether the member is acknowledging a fact, granting an immunity, or conceding statutory status as an 'interactive computer service provider'. The phrase is reasonably susceptible to more than one reading.

The passive-conduit acknowledgment cannot be squared with the very next paragraph of Section 13, which reserves the right 'to review and delete any Content that, in its sole judgment, violates' the Agreement, with Section 11's removal of reviews on resolution, and with Section 20's control over retention of ratings. The instrument describes Angie's List as both a passive carrier and an active editor of the Content.

'You agree that it is solely YOUR RESPONSIBILITY to evaluate Your risks to bear associated with the use ... of any Content that You submit' is garbled and, as written, applies the risk allocation to Content the member submits rather than Content the member reads. The mangled clause changes who bears what.

The reserved right 'to review and delete any Content that, in its sole judgment, violates' the Agreement is in tension with the immediately preceding passive-conduit acknowledgment in the same Section 13. A court asked whether Angie's List exercised editorial control would face both statements at once.

The disclaimer runs to Content, data, 'advertising', products, goods or services 'available or unavailable from, or through, any Service Providers', so it is genuinely uncertain whether it covers only third-party material or also Angie's List's own advertising and ratings presentation. The enumerated list against the qualifier 'from, or through, any Service Providers' is exactly the general-versus-specific tension a court must resolve.

Read against Section 1's description of the service and Section 13's passive-conduit and no-liability language, it is unclear whether Section 14 disclaims responsibility for Angie's List's own conduct in compiling and presenting ratings and advertising, or only for the Service Providers' conduct. The instrument as a whole does not settle which.

The release covers 'any interactions or dealings with any Service Provider' without saying whether Angie's List's own role in matching, rating or recommending that provider falls inside it. The breadth of 'interactions or dealings' is drafted entirely in the drafter's favour.

'Website Content' is defined to include 'information obtained from Angie's Lists, and other material contained on the Angie's List Website', which on its face sweeps in the reviews and ratings that Section 12 separately defines as 'Content'. The two defined terms overlap without a stated hierarchy.

The statement that posted health information goes 'into the public domain' and that no one has any obligation to keep it confidential is qualified only by 'Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement', which does not identify the qualifying provisions and sits against the Section 5 privacy policy. Which instrument governs the member's health data is left open.

Subsection (C) bars reviews Angie's List may consider 'unlawful, harassing, libelous ... distasteful ... or racially, ethnically or otherwise objectionable', a catch-all appended to a long specific list whose reach is indeterminate, and (D)'s requirement of 'thorough and thoughtful' reviews sets no applicable standard. The prohibited-conduct boundary cannot be fixed from the text.
Subsection (A) warrants that the member is 'above the age of eighteen (18)', which does not match Section 3's requirement of '18 years of age or older'. The two age gates differ by a year of members.

Limiting Angie's List to 'seeking damages' only 'if damages are ascertainable' sits against Section 27, which imposes fixed liquidated sums precisely 'because damages are often difficult to calculate'. The two remedies provisions rest on opposite premises.

Consent to transfer customer information 'to be used for any purpose allowed under this Agreement' has to be read against the Section 5 privacy policy, which is referenced but not expressly incorporated. Whether the policy limits the transferee's use is unresolved.

The initial term is said to be 'defined in Your membership Plan', but the Plans set out in Section 1 specify only monthly or annual billing and benefits, not a term. The provision points to a definition the instrument does not supply.

Termination is permitted 'for any reason in its sole discretion', yet the refund is owed only where Angie's List 'merely terminates Your account for its convenience' and the member 'is not in breach', and neither 'merely' nor 'convenience' is defined. Whether a discretionary termination is a convenience termination is left to construction.

Deletion of 'all related information and files' and possibly the member's Content on termination is difficult to reconcile with the Section 12 grant of an 'irrevocable, perpetual' licence and with Section 31, which keeps Section 12 in force after termination. Whether the Content survives termination is answered differently in the two places.

Modifications are 'effective immediately upon being posted' while the same paragraph promises 'You will receive notice if modifications ... are made', without saying whether notice conditions effectiveness or when it must be given. The two sentences pull in different directions within one provision.

Telling the member that the 'only recourse' for a disliked modification is to discontinue use is hard to square with Section 18's pro rata refund on convenience termination and with the paid annual term created by Section 6. A member locked into a prepaid year is left without the stated recourse.

An unqualified right to 'limit access to, modify, change or discontinue the Service' with no liability is hard to reconcile with the paid Plan benefits promised in Section 1 and the refund obligation in Section 18. Whether a member who has prepaid for a Plan can be deprived of it without remedy is unresolved.

'Submissions' are made Angie's List's property, but Section 12 defines 'Content' to include 'communications, information, data, text or other materials You give us' and disclaims ownership of it. A member comment could fall within both definitions, with opposite ownership consequences.

Disclaiming any warranty '(D) THAT ANY CONTENT OR INFORMATION YOU PROVIDE OR ANGIE'S LIST COLLECTS WILL NOT BE DISCLOSED' is in tension with the Section 5 privacy policy and the confidentiality assurances the member is directed to. Whether the privacy policy survives this disclaimer is left open.

Excluding all direct damages for '(G) ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT BY ANGIE'S LIST' and '(F) ANY OTHER MATTER RELATING TO THE SERVICE' would leave nothing for the very next paragraph's one-month cap to operate on, and would negate the Section 18 refund promise. The two liability provisions cannot both be given full effect.

The one-month cap presupposes that Angie's List may be 'FOUND LIABLE FOR ANYTHING RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT', whereas the preceding paragraph excludes liability for any breach of the Agreement altogether and Section 18 promises a pro rata refund that could exceed one month's fees. The provisions do not sit together.

The closing sentence — 'ANGIE'S LIST SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU UNDER THIS AGREEMENT' — reads as an affirmative assumption of liability against the blanket exclusions in the first paragraph of Section 25 and the releases in Sections 13 and 14. A member could rely on it as a residual liability undertaking.

In clause (c) it is unclear whether 'intentional or willful' modifies only 'violation of any rights of another' or also 'harm You may have caused to another', the latter reading making the member indemnify for merely negligent harm. The sentence supports both readings.

The liquidated sum is triggered where 'it becomes necessary for Angie's List to pursue legal action', yet subsection (A) fixes $1,000 'for each item of Content posted in violation', leaving unclear whether litigation is a condition and what counts as an 'item'. Both the trigger and the unit of computation are contestable.

Subsection (B) fixes $1,000 per item for displaying or copying 'any Content in violation of this Agreement', which overlaps subsection (A)'s $1,000 for posting Content in violation, so a single act may be charged twice. Section 27 does not say how the overlapping measures interact.

'Each review or record that is aggregated, disrupted, damaged or otherwise affected by You' has no ascertainable unit — 'otherwise affected' could reach every record on the site. The multiplier for the $100 charge is left open-ended.

Subsection (d) excepts 'the foregoing subsections (a) through (c)', but the subsections it refers to are lettered (A) through (C) in upper case, and it is unclear whether actual damages are available in addition to or instead of the liquidated sums. The interaction of the two remedies is not stated.

Notices to Angie's List are 'deemed delivered upon the earlier of the verification of delivery or two (2) business days after being sent', which conflicts with the Section 6 cancellation rule requiring the request to be 'received' by 5:00 p.m. the business day before renewal. A timely-deemed cancellation could still be treated as late.

The clause declares this Agreement the 'entire agreement' governing use of the Service, but does not say whether representations made on the website or in marketing about the ratings are within or outside 'the subject matter contained in this Agreement'. Integration clauses of this breadth are routinely construed against extrinsic representations.

The entire-agreement statement is hard to reconcile with the preamble, which binds the member to terms 'in, and linked to' the Agreement, and with the preamble's acknowledgment that other Angie's List sites may be governed by separate agreements and privacy policies. The instrument does not fix its own boundaries.

The forum is 'exclusive' for the member but the same sentence lets Angie's List 'elect, in its sole discretion' to sue elsewhere, so 'exclusive jurisdiction' does not mean what it says and the clause is wholly one-sided. Any genuine ambiguity in its reach would be construed against the drafter.

'Any claim or cause of action arising out or related to Your use of the Service or this Agreement' omits the word 'of' and, more importantly, gives no rule for when a claim 'arose', so the one-year period's starting point is undefined. Whether statutory consumer claims fall within 'related to' is also open.

The survival clause enumerates 'Sections 12, 14, 15, 17 and 23 through 31' but prefaces the list with 'including, but not limited to', so it is uncertain whether unlisted provisions such as Section 13's release survive termination. The catch-all sits directly against the enumeration.

The clause directs that a court 'should incorporate a similar provision that would be considered valid' rather than severing, which is a reformation instruction of uncertain content and effect. What counts as a 'similar' valid provision is left entirely open.

'Released Parties' is defined only in the credit-card paragraph of Section 25, so extending third-party-beneficiary status to 'each of the Released Parties' has a reach that depends on a definition given for a narrower purpose. Whether all credit-card-chain participants may enforce the whole Agreement is unclear.
